payload.description: What the wind-up of the council's housing company finally cost. Lion Homes (Norwich) Ltd could not repay £6.15m of loans that fell due on 31 March 2025 and went into a members' voluntary liquidation. The 2024/25 accounts say the council "has impaired the total amount of the loans to nil" and cut the value of its shareholding from £3.424m to £2.825m. The external auditor's finding on how the company came to be so little watched is on the record — "Based on the evidence available, there is no indication that adequate oversight arrangements for subsidiaries have ever existed, dating back to the subsidiary's incorporation in November 2015" — but no published document gives a final cost, and we will not publish an estimate of one.
